reviews.comment: Great professor. Super easy to make an A, hilarious, hardworking, and supportive! Take him!!

Choi is SO AWESOME! He keeps you engaged with funny stories, and relates the material to real-life disasters. If you need help, go see him in his office and he is super helpful. He tries really hard to help everyone get a good grade. Not a hard class if you pay attention in lecture and go to lab.

KC does a great job of turning a tough subject into something fun and engaging. He wants you to do well in his class. He's genuinely funny, and if you're willing to put in the effort, you'll definitely learn a lot.

KC is one of the most caring professors in the entire department. He finds a way to make lectures about a boring subject funny and engaging. He tells the funniest stories and somehow finds a way to make an analogy between that and the class content. Before every exam we were given a practice exam that was very similar to the real thing. Take KC.
KC Choi tries so hard to make a boring subject really enjoyable. Don't be afraid, he wants you to pass. Take him if you have the opportunity.

Choi is a funny guy. He does a good job teaching structures. I'll never forget watching a really low quality video on a building collapse interrupted by the "metal pipe falling sound effect". Bro is wild.

KC is my favorite professor. His enthusiasm, patience, humor, dedication. He gives after-class tutoring and rewards students in his unique way, encouraging steady progress.
He connects theory to life, simplifies complex concepts. His creative methods make learning easier. Moreover, he treats every student with respect and care.

KC is my favorite professor for his enthusiasm, humor, dedication. He give after-class tutoring and rewards students in his unique way, encouraging progress. He connects theory to daily life, simplfies complex concepts. His creative methods make learning easier. Moreover, he treats every student with respect and care, making him a beloved professor

COSC608 Structural Principles (statics). $12 workbook required for class work. HW was reviewed in class and graded after you made corrections. Attend class, be engaged, study your HW: you'll get an A. Dr. Choi was always available outside class for personal tutoring and invested in our success; amazing mentor and passionate about student success.

KC is a great professor! He was readily available to help with homework. I did not come from a construction or civil engineering background, so when I first walked into the structures class, I was very intimidated. However, during office hours, I would go to KC, and he would explain concepts and help me work through practice and homework problems.

This class is overall very challenging if taken with Estimating ll. KC was always there when I needed help and he always provided a lot of extra credit. Lectures are very entertaining but also hard to understand at times. There is a fair amount of homework, reviews are very similar to exams, and quizzes are extra credit. You can def pass this class

While he is hilarious and truly enjoys teaching this class, he is extremely hard to understand. He is an amazing person and always willing to help, but his accent makes it difficult to learn. Very similar to physics.

KC is a very engaging and funny teacher. He told us at the beginning that if you think you're bad at math not to worry and that he will build up your skills, and he is right. The material is not difficult, and he goes over multiple practice problems each lecture that really help. Would recommend taking this class with Estimating 2 if possible.
Professor Choi is incredibly passionate about his work. While the tests are hard, he makes it clear HOW to succeed.

KC had prepared for every possible scenario and offered his students several private tutoring sessions. His teaching style is very engaging and caring. The energy he brings truly lights up the class to do their best. With more than 190 students in a room, this is a truly impressive feat. When students were struggling, KC felt like hes failing.

Professor Choi is a great choice for COSC 321. My biggest takeaway is that had it not been online it would have been much more manageable. Lectures got you ready for the test. Homework was harder than the exams. I really encourage attending class because you have the opportunity to ask questions which makes it easier to understand the details.
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. KC in my opinion is awesome! I found COSC321 challenging but he made it possible. Dont get me wrong, in my downtime I had to review once and twice to understand the material but thats because I was a bit rusty. Dr. KC made it possible with a packet he created for the class, his continuous encouragement, and availability. Love the man!

He's honestly more of a college student than a prof. His grader and him are not the same page when grading Exams. The curves are pretty good in the class. You only needed a 74.5 to get a B in the class... Everything you learn in the class, you will NOT use in the construction industry.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Good!

Best professor in the program, takes time to help students, and truly cares about student success. Homework is very helpful for exam preparation. Lectures are highly engaging, hilarious and fun. I really appreciate the enthusiasm he had brought to class everyday.

Professor Choi is PASSIONATE about Structures and more importantly helping his students succeed. Attending class is a must to retain material and hear his very helpful tips/tricks . He is transparent about test material and gives lots of opportunities to receive help prior to exam days. Would love to take another class from KC.

I only made an A because I took physics last semester. A lot of people make C's. He can be extremely misleading. Multiple times he has not been available during his office hours, and sometimes his help desks do not even happen.

One of the best profs at A and M so far. Not an easy class, but quite rewarding. After taking the class, I truly feel as if I have learned something which you can't say about most professors at A and M lol.

It's pretty easy to tell this professor loves to teach. Pay attention in class, take good notes, find a group of friends to study with, and don't be afraid to ask questions. I wish he would teach Structures II.
Right off the bat, you can tell this professor loves to teach, because he's great at it. I wish he would teach COSC 421 because I would take him again.
Pushy on the term project. Too heavy workload. Good feedback. Want you publish a paper with his name involved.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He may be hard to understand at times, but he is very well prepared for class. Minus the fact that English is his second language, he does a good job making the complex understandable. He does plenty of examples in class and if you follow along you should be fine. His homework problems can be tough but they really prepare you for the test.

Go to class and pay attention, he is difficult to understand at times and has a tendency to go off on a tangent for 10+ minutes during class. Try to have an open mind, he is an incredibly intelligent man and wants his students to do well so be patient. For the tests, I practiced the homework assignments and I did very well in the class.

Cons: -Unclear in class -Lecture style is very fast-paced -Homework solutions given a only a few days before the exam -Unintentionally condescending by saying the following in class: every single problem in class is easy, if you're doing bad you're not working as hard as the students who are doing well  Pros: -Funny -Nice/Friendly
